_source_note: Recipes extracted from John Britt's self-published PDF 'Secrets of Oil Spot Glazes' (2024) - ingredient/percentage data only. Descriptions and notes above are written independently of the book's text, not copied from it. Wild/local materials (Sevier Shale, Vulcan Granite, Rotten Stone/Tripoli, Yellow Ochre, Burnt Umber) and commercial stain codes are not in this app's materials database and will show as unresolved ingredients rather than being silently substituted.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: John's SG-12
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Britt's primary go-to oil spot base, used with #4 Cover Glaze. A Redart/feldspar/ball clay body with dolomite and bone ash for magnesium.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: High Redart content (40%) causes shrinkage/cracking on drying; see John's SG-12 Calcined for the calcined-clay fix.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Cover Glaze
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Standard clear/amber cover applied over the base oil spot glazes to help differentiate the spots.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Applied 1-2 coats over 3-5 coats of the base oil spot glaze.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: John's SG-12 Calcined
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: SG-12 with part of the Redart pre-calcined to reduce drying shrinkage/cracking from the high clay content.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: 20.00% of the Red Art here is calcined separately (weighed raw, then calcined, or adjust for LOI) and combined with 20.12% raw Red Art.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Dorothy's SG-12 (FM Oil Spot)
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Albany-slip-based oil spot using soda feldspar and a small borax addition.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: SG-12 (original)
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: The original Albany-slip formulation that John's SG-12 was developed from after Albany Slip went out of production.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Originally used Albany Slip; the recipe works with Alberta, Redart or other iron slip clays substituted directly for the Albany.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Candace Black
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: High-iron, high-cobalt single-glaze oil spot - no separate cover needed. Britt's studio black glaze; the source of his original accidental oil-spot discovery.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Original recipe used 5% cobalt carbonate; Britt reduced it to 2%.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: SG-12 Match
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: A G-200/EPK-based oil spot with higher alumina, designed to be combined with crackle covers.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: John's Oil Spot
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Developed by blending Candace Black (too fluid when modified with more silica/kaolin) with a stiffer variant; a reliable, regularly-healing oil spot.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Original used 5% cobalt carbonate, cut to 2% (both work).

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: John's Oil Spot 3
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Works well in electric kilns. Slow-cooled (O3 or a comparable electric slow-cool) it can turn entirely silver as cobalt crystals grow and cover the piece.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Bailey's Oil Spot
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: A Tom Coleman-lineage feldspathic oil spot with a boron frit addition. Easy to use, rarely crawls, can produce large spots.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Traditional Oil Spot
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: A Tom Coleman recipe with no clay content at all - difficult to apply (needs bentonite) but produces classic results, especially double-fired oxidation then reduction. The calcined talc is essential.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: The talc must be calcined (heated to red heat, or included in a bisque firing) - this makes a significant difference. No clay in the recipe makes it difficult to apply; needs bentonite.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Montmollin Oil Spot
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: From Britt's High Fire book, contributed by French potter Daniel Montmollin (author of 'The Practice of Stoneware Glazes').

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Davis Oil Spot 1 (227)
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: A slip-based (Albany/Alberta) oil spot using burnt umber as an additional iron/manganese source.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Turns very silver when overfired then flash-cooled to cone 6.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Old Black Magic (OBM 1)
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: An oil spot with no magnesium source at all yet still spots well, using titanium dioxide instead of rutile.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Rotten Spot
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Uses Rotten Stone (Tripoli) as a silica-bearing flux component alongside a small wood ash and Barnard slip addition.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Talc should be calcined.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Mashiko Kaki 2
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: A Cornwall-Stone-based oil spot workable in both oxidation and reduction.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Davis OS/NAO 236
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Feldspar/slip/burnt-umber oil spot using old-style Buckingham potash feldspar (substitute G-200/Mahavir).

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Oil Spot 24
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Highest-alumina of the Currie-blend-derived Candace Black variants; drier and stiffer, yields smaller spots.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Developed from a Currie grid blend based on Candace Black, along with Oil Spot 28 and 29.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Oil Spot 28
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Middle Currie-blend variant of Candace Black; slightly less distinct spotting with some iron spangles.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Oil Spot 29
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Lowest-alumina Currie-blend variant of Candace Black; can produce large spots that run if applied too thick.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Fake Mashiko
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: 35% of the clay content pre-calcined (vs 20% in John's SG-12 Calcined), leaving very little raw clay to suspend the glaze - works fantastically despite the low raw-clay fraction. Tan/kaki in reduction, vigorous oil spot in oxidation.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: 35% of the Red Art listed here is calcined separately; only the 8.20% portion is raw clay. Credited to Chet McLaughlin via Britt's High Fire book.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Chinese Crackle
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Oil spot cover glaze derived from Kaun Crackle 1, using Zircopax instead of bone ash.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: For an iron-saturate version, drop the Zircopax and use 15% red iron oxide in its place.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Spotted Black
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Alberta-slip-based black glaze using yellow ochre as an additional iron source.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Yellow ochre sourcing varies widely; try different types.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Linda's Yellow
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: A feldspathic base carrying Mason 6433 yellow stain rather than iron oxide.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Bailey's Iron Red
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: High-bone-ash, lithium-fluxed oil spot for reds.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Real bone ash preferred over synthetic (TCP/tricalcium phosphate) if available.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Steve Irvine Red
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: High-bone-ash iron red with magnesium carbonate.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Snow Flake Crackle 1234
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: A feldspathic crackle cover with a small boron frit addition.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Randy Johnson's Temmoku
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Barium/zinc-fluxed temmoku with high-purity red iron.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Contains barium carbonate - not food safe as formulated.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Judi's Blue Crystal
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: High-dolomite, high-rutile crystal-matte-leaning glaze applied over oil spot bases; especially effective with an electric drop-and-hold cycle.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: John's Iron Saturate
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Simple, high-iron feldspathic saturate glaze, works in both oxidation and reduction.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Hamada Rust
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Gerstley-Borate-fluxed rust/iron glaze workable in either atmosphere.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: SLG-25
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Alberta-slip and nepheline base with a light-rutile crystal effect.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Mixed to specific gravity 150.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Rhodes 32
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Classic Daniel Rhodes magnesium/iron yellow, no zircopax, good in reduction.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Red iron oxide ranges 1-5% depending on desired depth.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Lau Luster Shino
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Nepheline/soda-ash shino used as an overglaze on fired oil spot tiles, refired.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Red iron oxide 2.5-3.0%. Applied over an already-fired oil spot (e.g. Candace Black) and refired.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Penn State Shino
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Spodumene-fluxed shino, reglazed over fired Candace Black and refired in reduction.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Red iron oxide 2.0-3.0%.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Button Gold
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Simple nepheline/redart/gerstley-borate base for the John's GB frit-substitution series below.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: John's GB-10
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Button Gold with Gerstley Borate replaced by 10% Ferro Frit 3269 (a substitute for the discontinued Frit P-25).

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: John's GB-15
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Button Gold series at 15% frit, retotaled.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: John's GB-20
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Button Gold series at 20% frit, retotaled.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: John's GB-25
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Button Gold series at 25% frit, retotaled.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: John's GB-30
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Button Gold series at 30% frit, retotaled.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: John's GB-35
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Button Gold series at 35% frit, retotaled - most fluid of the series.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: The GB-10 through GB-35 series are all Button Gold with increasing frit substitution (10-35%) for Gerstley Borate; each has a distinct look.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Meyer Shino
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Tin-opacified nepheline shino, similar base to Lau Luster with tin instead of extra iron.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Red Iron Wash
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: A brushable iron wash for use between or over glaze coats.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Cobalt Wash
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: A brushable cobalt wash for use between or over glaze coats.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Rutile Wash
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: A brushable rutile wash for use between or over glaze coats.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Burnt Umber Wash
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: A brushable pigment wash of pure burnt umber with a small clay/whiting binder addition.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Old Gold
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Alberta-slip base carrying a very heavy manganese dioxide and copper carbonate addition for a metallic gold effect.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Manganese dioxide (35%) and copper carbonate (15%) are additions on top of the 100% Custer/Alberta base, per the source - unusually heavy, defining this recipe's character rather than a minor colorant tweak.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Pinnell Manganese
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Feldspathic base carrying a very heavy manganese dioxide addition, with bentonite for suspension.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Manganese dioxide (29.3%), red iron oxide (0.8%) and bentonite (4%) are additions on top of the 100% base, per the source.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Pig Skin Temmoku
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: A wild-material temmoku using Britt's local Sevier Shale and Vulcan Granite alongside wood ash.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Sevier Shale and Vulcan Granite are Britt's own local materials (Johnson City, TN); no standard analysis available. Substitute a local iron-bearing shale/clay and granite dust, or see Johnson City OS for a Redart-substitutable version.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Johnson City OS
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: John's SG-12 with Sevier Shale substituted directly for Redart - demonstrates that most local iron-bearing clays work as a substitute in this base.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Sevier Shale is Britt's local material; substitute Redart or a comparable local iron-bearing clay.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Johnson City Temmoku
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Simple three-material temmoku built on local Sevier Shale.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Sevier Shale is Britt's local material (may not be obtainable); substitute Redart or a local clay.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: John's Ash
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Local shale, nepheline and wood ash - intended thin over oil spots.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Sevier Shale is Britt's local material; substitute Redart or a local clay if unavailable.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Albany Substitute (Krakowski)
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Lili Krakowski's Albany Slip substitute recipe - Britt's preferred one of the two he tested.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Not itself an oil spot glaze - a material substitute usable in place of Albany Slip in other recipes.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Albany Substitute (Hendley)
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: David Hendley's Albany Slip substitute recipe - Britt's second-choice alternative.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Not itself an oil spot glaze - a material substitute usable in place of Albany Slip in other recipes.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Candace Black (Cone 6)
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Candace Black adapted to cone 6 with a Frit 3110 addition for lower-temperature melting.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Britt suggests Frit 3134 instead of 3110 might improve results (adds more boron).

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Oil Spot Combo 1
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Cone 6 base layer for the Oil Spot Combo pairing (apply Combo 2 cover over this).

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Oil Spot Combo 2 (Cover)
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Cone 6 zircon-opacified cover for Oil Spot Combo 1, with several stain/oxide color variants.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Color variants (add on top of base): 5% Mason 6485 yellow; 5% Mason 6001 pink; 5% Mason 6363 blue; 4% Degussa yellow stain + 2% cobalt carbonate; 2% each copper carbonate/cobalt carbonate/chrome oxide; 8% red iron oxide; 2% chrome oxide; 2% nickel oxide.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Licorice
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: A genuine cone 5/6 oil spot (most cone 6 'oil spots' in this book rely on stains rather than true thermal iron reduction - this one uses real red iron oxide). Enhanced with a white cover and a slow-cool schedule.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Mix to specific gravity 150-155; apply 2-3 coats in a tiered manner. Best with a white cover glaze and a slow-cool electric schedule.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: John's Brown
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Licorice with the cobalt carbonate omitted - a revised brown version.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Mix to specific gravity 150-155; apply 2-3 coats in a tiered manner.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Pierre's Temmoku
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: High-iron cone 6 temmoku base for the Pierre's pairing.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Pierre's Cover
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Frit-fluxed cone 6 cover glaze paired with Pierre's Temmoku.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Vickery OS1
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Cone 6 base layer for the Vickery pairing.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: Vickery Cover 2
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Zircon-opacified Gerstley Borate cover for Vickery OS1, with a stain variant option.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Alternative: substitute the 10% Zircopax with 10% Mason Stain 6200.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: OS1
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: A simpler G-200-based cone 6 oil spot base, close relative of Vickery OS1.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: OS Combo 2
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Gerstley-borate cover glaze for the OS1 pairing, with an optional Mason stain addition.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Optional: add up to 5% Mason stain of choice.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: John's Spotted Black
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Not a true oil spot (no iron oxide) - a revised satin matte base carrying Mason 6612 Onyx Black, which bubbles similarly to oil spots when fired. A cone 5 revision of Britt's Charcoal Satin Matte.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Mix to specific gravity 150-155; apply 2-3 coats in a tiered manner. Best under John's Crystal White/Yellow Matte cover with a slow-cool electric schedule.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: John's Spotted Red
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Same charcoal-satin-matte base as John's Spotted Black, carrying an inclusion stain (e.g. Rose, Green, Orange, Tangerine) instead of black.

variations.name: John's Spotted Red (rose)
variations.expected_color: rose/red (10% inclusion stain, e.g. #1352 Rose from Uspigment.com)

britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Mix to specific gravity 150-155; apply 3 coats in a tiered manner. Britt notes several inclusion-stain color variants (rose, green, orange, tangerine) using the same base.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: John's Crystal White Matte
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: Talc-heavy zinc matte cover for the spotted-glaze series; a slight variant of Britt's 'Autumn's Crystal Matte' from his Mid-Range book.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Mix to specific gravity 145; apply thin, 1-2 coats - will blister if too thick.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: John's Crystal Yellow Matte
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: John's Crystal White Matte with Mason 6485 yellow stain added.

britt_oil_spot_glazes.name: John's Rutile
britt_oil_spot_glazes.description: The Charcoal-Satin-Matte-derived liner glaze for the spotted series, without any stain added.
britt_oil_spot_glazes.notes: Mix to specific gravity 150-155; apply 1-2 coats.
